item.title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
item.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December. item.title: Rutgers Guard Kwabena Asamoah to Miss the Rest of the Season with Injury
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NJ - NOVEMBER 19: Rutgers Scarlet Knights offensive lineman Kwabena Asamoah (69) during the college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Penn State Nittany Lions on November 19, 2022 at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers Star guard Kwabena Asamoah will miss the rest of the season due to surgery he had for a high ankle sprain, according to 247Sports’ Bobby Deren. Asamoah, who chose to return to Rutgers for his fifth year, has played in 48 total games for the program. Unortantely due to the injury, he played his last game in a Scarlet Knight uniform as he is now out of eligibility. According to multiple reports, he is expected to make a full recovery and continue football training in January so that he is ready for the NFL Draft. Asamoah achieved several notable accolades during his Rutgers career, including being named team captain in 2026, being an All-Big Ten honorable mention in 2024 and 2025, as well as earning second-team All-America by ESPN in 2025. He also cleared the way for three 1,000-yard rushers during his career, blocking for Kyle Monangai and Antwan Raymond, who rushed for over 1,000 yards in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Through eight games of 2026, Asamoah played 498 snaps at right guard. Over that time, he allowed only three total pressures, which is tied for the fourth-fewest in the country among guards who have played at least 400 snaps. His list of consecutive starts was one of the longest on the team, as he started every game in 2024, 2025, and the first eight games in 2026. With his college career now over, Asamoah will look to recover quickly and prepare for the NFL Draft. In addition to Asamoah being ruled out for the season, star wide receiver KJ Duff has been ruled out for the Knights’ upcoming game against Wisconsin. His injury has been deemed a lower-body injury, but specifics have not been released. Last week, Duff left the game against Michigan early due to the injury. These two, combined with starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan being out for the game, mean that Rutgers will be taking on Wisconsin without several key pieces on offense.

item.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
item.description: Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds . Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs. VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn’t even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free. “The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR,” said the Premier League Match Centre. Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/fuK42Okkcz — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026 The statement added VAR Tony Harrington’s verdict to Brooks: “I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”. The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and expressed his displeasure again when Pedro Porro was booked for a similar foul after the break, with the Italian booked for his reaction. Roberto De Zerbi was booked for his reaction after Pedro Porro was cautioned for a similar tackle to Jayden Bogle’s (Reuters) “Pedro Porro's was a duel and an incredible yellow card. The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing,” De Zerbi told TNT Sports , before stopping short of criticising the officials. Asked if the referee should have gone to the monitor to review Bogle’s challenge, he said: "No. I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve." De Zerbi’s woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes. Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win. Mathys Tel was forced off during Tottenham's clash with Leeds (Getty) De Zerbi’s attacking options have already been ravaged by injury this season and the club will now be left to sweat over the extent of Tel’s setback. Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk are out until after the international break, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are continuing to work their way back from serious knee injuries, with both eyeing returns after the turn of the year. Tel has impressed for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring a stunning solo goal in their 2-0 win over Chelsea on 24 October, the club’s first victory at Stamford Bridge

item.title: Maryvale football wins first playoff game in 21 years
item.description: For the first time in 21 years, the Maryvale Panthers have won a playoff game. No. 13 Phoenix Maryvale shut out the No. 20 ALA West Foothills Guardians, 35-0, in a first-round 4A high school football playoff game on Friday, Nov. 6. The Panthers used a stifling defense to secure three takeaways and consistently give the offense a short field. Key Plays The Panthers scored their first touchdown of the game when freshman quarterback Marcus Escobedo Jr. found Miles Woods for a 14-yard score with 5:16 to go in the first. Maryvale junior running back Isaac Buchanan scored the first of his two touchdowns after a 25-yard run reached pay dirt with 7:15 to go in the second quarter. Escobedo Jr. found the end zone after a nifty red zone scramble and crossed the pylon with just seconds before the first half ended, putting the Panthers up 21-0. Buchanan scored the final touchdown of the game scoring from a yard out after a 35-yard catch and run from Woods set them up with a goal to go at the 1 yardline. Key Players Maryvale's Escobedo Jr. finished the game throwing for 209 yards and a touchdown on 11 of 15 passing. He also added a rushing touchdown. Woods caught five passes for 135 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 27 yards a catch in Friday's contest. Junior RB Buchanan had a workhorse performance rushing for 67 yards on 16 carries and scoring two touchdowns. Quotes "Tonight we blanked a really good football team," Maryvale co-head coach Marcus Carter said. "We're physical, we're fast, we're young and these kids are sponges and they're hungry. To pitch a shutout against a really good ALA west team is a statement." "Our freshman QB has poise," Maryvale co-head coach Mark Carter said. "He could have gone to any school, he decided to come here, we feel blessed to have him and he's only going to get better." "We just couldn't get that spark," ALA West Foothill head coach Bryan Rauzen said. "We're going to miss these seniors a lot but I can positively say we are building a tradition here." Up next Maryvale (10-1) will travel to Prescott, to face No. 4 Bradshaw Mountain (7-3) in the second round on Nov. 13. The Bears had a first-round bye. The season ended Friday for ALA West Foothills. item.title: MLS Decision Day Rondo: Can Nashville SC make history? Will LA Galaxy and the Seattle Sounders avoid playoff disaster?
item.description: MLS winners and losers GFX - GOAL A points record within reach, seasons on the brink and star names under pressure: GOAL’s writers debate who will rise - and who could fall - on MLS Decision Day. Right, so, Decision Day time. For those uninitiated, this is basically where all of the MLS games kick off at the same time on the final day of the regular season. In an ideal world, there are still loads of possible permutations and combinations as to who makes the playoffs and how. Decision Day is supposed to be, well, decisive. And this year, it might just be lacking a bit of spark. The East, from a 'who makes it' POV is sewn up. The West has a little wildcard jeopardy, but basically we're looking at one or two sides falling out of the picture late on. However, there is some drama to be found. Nashville SC tied the single-season points record last week. Any sort of result against FC Cincinnati on Saturday, and they will set a new one. And even if the West isn't all that pumping, having a number of games kick off at the same time means things will fluctuate throughout the night. So, what does this all look like? And does this year's Decision Day feel as decisive as it should? GOAL writers break it down in another edition of... The Rondo . Will Nashville SC set a points record this weekend? Hany Mukhtar has been magnificent in Nashville's record-breaking season. Tom Hindle : Why not?! Sure, after securing the Supporters' Shield and tying a record, B.J. Callaghan might be tempted to rest some of his guys and make sure nothing goes too wrong. But their opponent, FC Cincinnati, are more or less locked where they're at. The smart money, based on this season? Nashville concede and then mount a furious late comeback. Alex Labidou: It’s been a regular season of destiny for the Boys in Gold , so why would that change on Decision Day? I fully expect Nashville to finish the job Saturday and claim the points record. Ryan Tolmich: It’ll be tough considering Cincinnati will have something to play for. Even so, Nashville are the best team in MLS, so it would be silly to bet against them. Which two Western Conference teams will secure wild card slots? Brian Schmetzer's Seattle Sounders shouldn't be counted out in the West playoff hunt TH : Wow, it's tight. But let's assume the results shake out in the way they should , and it will be Seattle and Colorado in a wildcard slot, with LA Galaxy sliding in at seventh place. Minnesota United have been magnificent of late, but they will need help from elsewhere, and San Jose are a tough opponent. No miracle for the Loons . AL: This is tough, but it’s hard to imagine Brian Schmetzer and the Seattle Sounders missing the playoffs. I’m banking on the Rave Green to secure one spot. While Colorado and the LA Galaxy have more talent than Portland, the Timbers have the most favorable Decision Day matchup: a hapless Austin FC side sitting 14th. On that basis, I’m backing Portland to get in, too. RT: The odds are heavily against Seattle

item.title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen to have penalties
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc will both have 10-place grid penalties in Sao Paulo on Sunday [Getty Images] Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Verstappen will start from the back of the grid while Hamilton and Leclerc will both have 10-place penalties. They join Mercedes driver George Russell in having penalties for using too many engine parts. Russell's drop is only five places. Verstappen will have an an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc, Hamilton and Russell have all fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalties for the Ferrari drivers are bigger than Russell's because it is the first time they have exceeded the limit of four engines per season, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Rain is predicted overnight from Saturday into Sunday in the city this year, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." item.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Max Verstappen edges out Kimi Antonelli in FP3
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen set the fastest time in Free Practice 3 at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, narrowly edging out Kimi Antonelli as Lewis Hamilton ’s Ferrari suffered a mechanical issue. The impending threat of rain meant all drivers rushed onto the track – especially Nico Hulkenberg , whose Audi suffered a terminal issue at the hands of rookie Freddie Slater in FP1, preventing him from partaking in the second session at all. These laps were therefore the German’s first this weekend. Everyone focused on the medium tyre compound in the opening 40 minutes of the session, Kimi Antonelli fastest in 1m12.209s, leading Verstappen by 0.075s – despite the new world champion reporting a steering wheel problem, while the four-time title winner reported his steering was “heavy to the right”. Charles Leclerc was third, 0.230s adrift, while George Russell , Liam Lawson and Oscar Piastri were half a second down on Antonelli. Lawson, who set the fastest time in sector three, was nearly 0.5s quicker than Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad and almost one second faster than any other midfield driver. Hamilton, who reported “strange vibrations” emanating from his new powertrain and “big engine braking”, was just eighth-fastest ahead of Hadjar, who described his RB22 as “close to undriveable”. The Ferrari man’s issue would later lead to “smoke in the cockpit” amid a worrying sound. As the field switched to soft rubber, Verstappen narrowly edged out Antonelli to set the fastest time, with a 1m11.622s to the Mercedes driver’s 1m11.647s. Lando Norris hauled his McLaren up to third, 0.131s adrift, followed by Russell and Leclerc – meaning the four top teams lapped within 0.274s. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes This time, Lindblad was one tenth quicker than Lawson, with the pair again roughly half a second faster than Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Alpine ’s Pierre Gasly in the midfield. Hadjar also ended up behind both Racing Bulls in the classification, with a 0.591s deficit to pacesetter Verstappen. Hamilton’s issue meant he was confined to the garage and performed no soft-tyre run, ending up 12th in the final results. Debutant Rafael Camara was 15th-fastest, 0.128s quicker than team-mate Oliver Bearman . Lance Stroll propped up the order after encountering a suspected ERS issue 15 minutes into the session, which proved terminal. item.title: Former Real Madrid star opines on Vinicius’ situation: ‘They play better with Diomande’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star opines on Vinicius’ situation: ‘They play better with Diomande’ Vinicius Jr.’s spot in Real Madrid’s starting XI is now under serious threat, or, for practical purposes, may well be gone. The long-term suspension has not helped the player’s case in any way after his poor start to the season. Some saw it as a much-needed reset for the Brazilian star, but as he prepared to return to league action after the international break, he will find Yan Diomande sitting comfortably ahead of him as Jose Mourinho’s preferred option on the left wing. Former player speaks on Vinicius Former Real Madrid and Spain striker Fernando Morientes spoke to the media earlier this week, where he opened up with his honest assessment of Vinicius Jr.’s situation and his competition with Yan Diomande. Tough times for Vinicius Jr. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Sharing his honest thoughts on the same, Morientes admitted that Vinicius was not quite at the level that he is usually associated with, as he said (h/t Defensa Central ): “We are not looking at the best version of Vinicius at the moment, but, well, that is the reality. I think he himself has acknowledged it, hasn’t he?” He then stressed that it was the responsibility of the coaching staff to ensure the player returns to his best. “The responsibility of the coaching staff, without getting into the wider debate, is to try to bring back the best version of Vinicius,” he began. “Especially considering that his current performances have fallen short of what is expected from a player of his stature, given his history at Real Madrid and his most recent contract renewal,” he added. “The coaching staff’s job is to work towards that without fuelling all the external debate surrounding him,” he concluded. Morientes then backed Yan Diomande as Real Madrid’s superior left-wing option at this point in time. Diomande has utilised his chances well. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “The reality today is that Diomande is in better form, and Real Madrid currently play better with Diomande on the left than they do with Vinicius. “At the same time, however, the coaching staff’s responsibility is to bring back Vinicius’s best version.” On what lies ahead for Vinicius The former striker then backed Vinicius to come good and insisted that he is still a decent player who can contribute, even until he returns to his best. “I believe he is a player who can still contribute. I believe he is an important player, and I don’t think we should write him off, because players like him can be decisive when they are in top form.” “When a player like Vinicius, whose strengths are taking on defenders, dribbling and scoring goals, fails to deliver those qualities, his shortcomings become much more noticeable than those of other players,” he added. item.title: NBC solicits Brent Musburger, Bob Costas to narrate opening tease for Miami-Notre Dame
item.description: Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NBC Sports is giving Saturday’s Miami-Notre Dame matchup the big-game treatment with one of the network’s famous pregame teases. Before the Hurricanes and Fighting Irish kick off from South Bend at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, the network will give viewers a brief history of the recently renewed rivalry in the trademark style NBC Sports is known for. The opening tease begins with clips of Jimmy Johnson’s and Lou Holtz’s Miami and Notre Dame teams at the inception of what is now colloquially known as Catholics vs. Convicts before transitioning to the modern day, when a three-point Miami win in Week 1 of the 2025 season proved to be the difference between which team earned the final bid into the College Football Playoff just a year ago. And to add to the stakes, NBC has tapped two heavyweights to narrate the package. Brent Musburger, who called the original Catholics vs. Convicts game for CBS in 1988, narrates the tease alongside Bob Costas, who has lent his voice to many of NBC’s trademark opens throughout his time with the network. NBC has leaned into its history of producing narrative-setting opens for big games of late, particularly since the NBA returned to its airwaves last year. Many associate the style of these packages, and Costas’ voice, with Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls dynasty in the ’90s, and NBC Sports dutifully brought them back last NBA season to heaping praise. Now, the network will go back to the well for what is arguably the biggest college football game it will air all season. item.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc hit with Sao Paulo grid penalties in more Ferrari misery
item.description: Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix . The Ferrari duo have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA. The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday evening after Hamilton’s fury over his team-mate’s lap-one overtake on him in Mexico. Lewis Hamilton drives past a mural of Ayrton Senna in Sao Paulo (Bradley Collyer/PA) Hamilton questioned Leclerc’s mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks. Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend’s race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components. It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024. Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday’s race being affected. Formula One announced a five-year extension for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

item.title: Guernsey FC keep up winning run with 4-0 Lancing victory
item.description: Guernsey captain Ross Allen opened the scoring early on [BBC] Guernsey FC made it six successive wins in the Southern Combination Premier Division as they beat Lancing 4-0 at Victoria Park. item.title: Are the Badgers right to make a QB change to Ryan Hopkins?
item.description: MADISON, WI - SEPTEMBER 12: Wisconsin quarterback Ryan Hopkins (10) hands the ball off to Wisconsin running back Bryan Jackson II (21) during a college football game between the University of Wisconsin Badgers and the Western Illinois University Leathernecks on September 12, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Lawrence Iles/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are finally making a change at quarterback, as Ryan Hopkins will get his first career start against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, and looks to have the green light for Wisconsin’s final four games of the season. The Badgers, sitting at 5-3, have really struggled to throw the ball with starter Colton Joseph, who has completed under 56 percent of his passes this season, and has gone for fewer than 100 passing yards in three straight outings. The roughest one came last weekend against the Iowa Hawkeyes, as Joseph completed just 5 of 14 passes before being benched for Hopkins for the fourth quarter. Coming out of that game, Hopkins remains the starter, which a majority of fans looked for in our weekly Reacts poll. Wisconsin now faces Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue, and Minnesota in its final four games, so it should get an accurate look at Hopkins before making a key quarterback decision for the 2027 season. Was this the right time to make the quarterback change? Just a week ago, we saw reports that Wisconsin was negotiating with Colton Joseph for the 2027 season. But now, that feels unlikely, and it comes down to a rough transfer portal evaluation. Joseph just never improved the way the Badgers wanted him to, as accuracy and footwork issues were prevalent from the offseason and have carried throughout the year. He was a major work in progress coming into the season with his passing inconsistencies at Old Dominion, but his rushing ability was expected to provide a quality floor in the Big Ten. Still, Wisconsin’s offense has struggled a good amount, and moving to Hopkins feels like a much-needed move here at the end of the season. With jobs at stake, Wisconsin needs to see if Hopkins can be its guy next season or whether it’ll need to evaluate outside the program for its starter next year. At the very least, Hopkins looked confident as a passer last week, while dealing with some rookie mistakes. If he can build on that, Wisconsin has a chance to finish this season strong. It all starts on Saturday, when the Badgers take on Rutgers as 19.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel. But it’s another missed quarterback evaluation for the Badgers, and one that should create a lot of questions on process in the offseason.

item.description: Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images Chris Bosh believes the lack of preseason games has been one of the reasons behind the rise of injuries in the NBA. The Hall of Famer played 70 or more games eight times in his career, which is a sensational achievement. In the current NBA, with injuries rising, not a lot of people are able to compete in a large number of games. Already, players like Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Anthony Edwards and Paolo Banchero are set to miss months due to injuries, which has led to an outcry among many to reduce the number of games per season. There has been no decision regarding the number of games being reduced, but the belief is that Adam Silver could be interested in trimming the game down to 40 minutes. No guarantee that playing fewer minutes will completely take away injuries, but Bosh knows what has led to the rise in injuries. Chris Bosh speaks on the importance of preseason The number of preseason games has reduced significantly in the past few years. CBA rules suggest that teams will not be allowed to play more than six preseason games. Despite this, very few teams use the full quota, and on average, franchises just give their players 3 to 5 games in the preseason. “I saw something really interesting over the weekend on RJ’s podcast, and he was speaking of how guys, especially the superstar guys, right? The guys who the team have paid them all their money to lead them, to score all the points, get all the rebounds, be the superstars that they are. And we expect these guys, going from a short training camp, only playing about one or two preseason games, to playing big minutes at a higher level, faster level, once the regular season starts. And that’s definitely a mistake,” said Bosh in a video that he uploaded online. “Before, we had eight preseason games. Maybe eight’s too much. I don’t know.
